0.0.n: A Japanese family name, used here to address the other person.

0.1.n: Added after a name to show respect; it does not specify gender.

0.3.n: A given name written in katakana, the script commonly used for foreign names.

0.4.n: Marks the name being given before 言います.

0.5.n: Polite form of 言う; with a name and と, it introduces the speaker.

1.0.n: A Japanese family name, given here as the speaker's own name.

1.1.n: Marks the name being given before 言います.

1.2.n: Polite form of 言う, used here to introduce oneself.

2.0.n: Pairs with お願いします in a standard greeting that asks for goodwill.

2.1.n: A polite request expression; with よろしく, it becomes a conventional introduction greeting.

3.0.n: Pairs with お願いします to return the other person's friendly introduction greeting.

3.1.n: A polite request expression; the whole phrase expresses goodwill when meeting someone.

4.0.n: Names the dish whose preparation the speaker is discussing.

4.1.n: Makes ramen the topic, setting it apart as the dish under discussion.

4.2.n: Past form of 作る; before こと, it refers to the experience of making something.

4.3.n: Turns 作った into an experience; the usual following particle が is omitted in this conversational sentence.

4.4.n: Polite negative of ある; after a past verb and こと, it expresses never having had that experience.

5.0.n: Strengthens the negative 詳しくないです, emphasizing a complete lack of familiarity.

5.1.n: 詳しい changes to 詳しくない for the negative; です makes the statement polite.

5.3.n: Strengthens 知らないです, emphasizing that the speaker knows nothing about the subject.

5.4.n: 知らない is the negative of 知る; adding です makes it polite.

5.6.n: The て-form of 教える plus ください makes a polite request; the learner and subject are understood.

6.0.n: Acknowledges the request before offering reassurance.

6.2.n: A neutral, polite way to refer to oneself; に marks this person as the one entrusted.

6.3.n: Marks 私 as the person who will take responsibility.

6.4.n: The て-form of 任せる plus ください politely asks the listener to entrust the task to the speaker.

6.6.n: A casual, emphatic expression conveying confidence that everything will go well.

6.7.n: Adds politeness to the casual reassurance バッチリ.

7.0.n: Here it signals reliance on the other person's help, rather than introducing oneself.

7.1.n: With よろしく, it politely accepts the offer of help and expresses goodwill in advance.

0.tip: Name + と言います is a polite way to introduce yourself; the subject I is usually omitted.

1.tip: Do not add さん to your own name when introducing yourself.

2.tip: Treat よろしくお願いします as a set greeting expressing goodwill, not as a literal request.

3.tip: Repeating よろしくお願いします is a natural way to return this introduction greeting.

4.lit: As for ramen, the experience of having made it does not exist.
4.tip: Past verb + ことがありません means you have never done something; が is dropped here.

5.lit: I am not knowledgeable at all. I do not know at all. Please teach me.
5.tip: 全く strengthens a negative statement, like not at all in English.

6.lit: Yes, please entrust it to me. It is all set.
6.tip: 私に任せてください is a reassuring way to tell someone to leave a task to you.

7.tip: After an offer of help, よろしくお願いします conveys that you are counting on the person and appreciate their help.
